title: Chip stocks are caught in a $1 trillion wipeout. Here's what's going on.
key_facts: Large chip and memory stocks lost more than $1 trillion in market value this week as investors sold for a second day on Thursday.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down 12% from its early-October peak and was heading for a seventh straight losing day, its worst streak since May 2025.
Selling began in South Korea, where SK Hynix and Samsung are more than half of the Kospi's value, and spread to Japan and the US.
Triggers named: Chinese firm CXMT saying it advanced a denser memory chip design; September US inflation of 3.7% against 3.6% expected; producer prices up 6.3% a year.
Markets price a 92% chance the Fed raises rates at least once more by year end; the 10-year Treasury yield fell 13 basis points to 5.06%.
CoreWeave's bonds due 2032 rose from 9.625% at issue in June to almost 15% this week; hyperscalers are on track for about $800 billion of capex this year, per Goldman Sachs.
JPMorgan strategists floated a possible 'inflection point' for chip stocks, which remain about 15% below June highs.
quote_evidence: Investors dumped high-flying chip and memory stocks for a second day on Thursday, with the largest names in the sectors shedding more than $1 trillion in market cap this week.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down 12% from its peak in early October.
Some analysts are eyeing the possibility that the chips rout may be nearing its end.
why_it_matters_hint: A fast chip sell-off tied to AI spending doubts, hot inflation and rate-hike bets.
